title: Supabase Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Supabase course.

entries.name: Know the database and the client
entries.summary: Supabase stores table data in PostgreSQL and exposes APIs around it.

example.code:
Browser page -> Supabase API -> PostgreSQL table
The public client key identifies the project.
Row-level security decides which rows the client role may access.

entries.name: Create a local sample table
entries.summary: A PostgreSQL table defines the fields used by the API.

example.code: CREATE TABLE public.cma_books(id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,title text NOT NULL,pages integer CHECK(pages>0));

entries.name: Seed public sample records
entries.summary: Seed data is a small set of known records used for learning or testing.

example.code: INSERT INTO public.cma_books(title,pages) VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Garden Days',40),('Tiny Seed',20);

entries.name: Enable row-level security
entries.summary: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles.

example.code: ALTER TABLE public.cma_books ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

entries.name: Allow only the public read
entries.summary: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role.

example.code:
GRANT SELECT ON public.cma_books TO anon;
CREATE POLICY "Read public sample books" ON public.cma_books FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true);

entries.name: Make a local client
entries.summary: createClient connects the JavaScript SDK to the chosen project API.

entries.name: Select named columns
entries.summary: A select request can ask only for the columns a page needs.

entries.name: Filter with a comparison
entries.summary: The client can add a filter to a query. gte means greater than or equal to.

entries.name: Order and limit the result
entries.summary: Ordering and limiting help a page request a small useful set.

entries.name: Count without requesting every row
entries.summary: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out.

entries.name: Expect a denied write
entries.summary: A read-only policy should reject browser writes.

entries.name: Keep environments separate
entries.summary: Local and hosted projects have different addresses and keys.

example.code:
Local development: local URL, local public key, fictional sample rows.
Hosted app: its own public URL/key and reviewed policies.
Server-only operations: secret key kept out of browser bundles.
Before running changes: verify which project the client points to.
